subject.title: [Architecture] Enforce strict typings for command payloads in packages/gateway-protocol

question: Should Gateway dispatch adopt a schema-derived typed handler map for built-in methods while preserving a separate typed or generic plugin registration seam?
rationale: The runtime-validation concern is real, but the permanent type boundary affects core dispatch, generated protocol types, and plugin-registered methods; source inspection cannot choose that public extension contract safely.

options.title: Stage typed core handlers
options.body: Introduce a schema-derived built-in method map, keep plugin methods behind an explicit extension contract, and migrate handler families in bounded PRs.

options.title: Keep generic dispatch
options.body: Retain runtime validation plus generic handler params and address only specific unsafe assertions when they cause concrete defects.

options.title: Defer to SDK design
options.body: Wait for the broader public Gateway SDK and type-map direction before changing internal handler contracts.

recommendation.title: Stage typed core handlers
recommendation.body: Introduce a schema-derived built-in method map, keep plugin methods behind an explicit extension contract, and migrate handler families in bounded PRs.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history signal connects steipete to recent Gateway documentation and repository architecture direction, making them the best low-confidence owner for this boundary decision.
